start.README.md:
# Triptych

A sliding-tile merge game on a 4x4 board in the 2048 family, except that tiles merge in triples of 3. The engine is headless: a `Game`, its legal moves and exact text for every reply.

## The board

The board has 4 rows and 4 columns, numbered from 0, row 0 at the top. Every other cell is empty or holds a tile with a positive value; tile values are powers of 3 (1, 3, 9, ...).

## Moves

A move is one of the strings `L`, `R`, `U`, `D` (slide left, right, up, down; upper case only). A move is *legal* exactly when it changes the board; a move that would change nothing is illegal (and so is every other string). A legal move does, in this order: slide and merge (below), add the merge points to the score, count the move, spawn one tile.

### Sliding and merging

Lines move independently: every row for `L`/`R` and every column for `U`/`D` is a *line*. Take a segment and read its tiles (skipping the empty cells) starting from the end nearest to the side the tiles move towards (the left end for `L`, the right end for `R`, the top for `U`, the bottom for `D`). Walk through that list from its start: if the next 3 tiles are all equal to some value `v`, they merge into one tile of value `3*v` and the walk continues after them; otherwise the tile stays as it is and the walk continues with the next one. The resulting tiles are packed against the same end of the segment, in the same order, and the rest of the segment is empty. A tile created by a merge is never merged again in the same move. The score gains the value of every tile created by a merge.

Example on a line of 4 cells: `1 1 1 1` moved left becomes `3 1 . .` (score +3); moved right it becomes `. . 1 3` (score +3).

### Spawning

The generator is MINSTD: `state = state * 48271 mod 2147483647`, and `next()` returns the new state. `NewGame(seed)` starts with `state = seed mod 2147483647`, or `1` if that is 0.

A spawn first lists the candidate cells in row-major order (row 0 first, left to right): the cells that are empty and not walls. Then `i = (next() >> 8) mod (number of candidates)` picks the i-th candidate (0-based), and a second call decides the value: `1` normally, `3` when `(next() >> 8) mod 8 == 0`. The position is drawn before the value; nothing else ever calls `next()`. A new game spawns twice (two tiles) before the first move; every legal move spawns once, after the slide.

Check: with seed 1 the first four values of `next()` are 48271, 182605794, 1291394886, 1914720637.

## Rules of the game

The game is *over* when no move is legal. The first line of the board text carries ` WIN` when the largest tile is at least 81 and ` OVER` when the game is over (play simply continues after a win).

## API (package `triptych`)

```go
g := triptych.NewGame(seed uint32)
g.LegalMoves() []string          // the legal moves, in any order; empty when the game is over
g.Apply(move string) (string, error) // plays a legal move and returns the event; an error, and no change, otherwise
g.Render() string                // the board text (below)
g.Score() int
g.Over() bool
```

### Event returned by `Apply`

`+<points> spawn <row>,<col>=<value>`: the score gained by the move and the tile that spawned, for example `+9 spawn 2,0=1` (rows and columns from 0).

### `Render()`

The first line is `score <score> moves <moves>` followed by ` WIN` and/or ` OVER` when they apply (in that order). Then one line per row, no trailing newline at the end of the text. Every cell is written as its value (`.` for an empty cell, `#` for a wall), right-aligned to the width `w` = the number of digits of the largest tile on the board (at least 1), and the cells of a row are joined by a single space. Example (a board whose largest tile is 81):

```
score 90 moves 21
 .  3  .  1
81  .  9  .
 .  .  1  .
 3  .  .  .
```

## Tests

`go test ./...` replays the scenario files in `testdata/` (`adapter_test.go` shows how the API is called; the format is described at the top of `scenarios_test.go`).

start.README.md:
# Triptych

A sliding-tile merge game on a 4x4 board in the 2048 family, except that tiles merge in pairs of 2. The engine is headless: a `Game`, its legal moves and exact text for every reply.

## The board

The board has 4 rows and 4 columns, numbered from 0, row 0 at the top. Every other cell is empty or holds a tile with a positive value; tile values are powers of 2 (1, 2, 4, ...).

## Moves

A move is one of the strings `L`, `R`, `U`, `D` (slide left, right, up, down; upper case only). A move is *legal* exactly when it changes the board; a move that would change nothing is illegal (and so is every other string). A legal move does, in this order: slide and merge (below), add the merge points to the score, count the move, spawn one tile.

### Sliding and merging

Lines move independently: every row for `L`/`R` and every column for `U`/`D` is a *line*. Take a segment and read its tiles (skipping the empty cells) starting from the end nearest to the side the tiles move towards (the left end for `L`, the right end for `R`, the top for `U`, the bottom for `D`). Walk through that list from its start: if the next 2 tiles are all equal to some value `v`, they merge into one tile of value `2*v` and the walk continues after them; otherwise the tile stays as it is and the walk continues with the next one. The resulting tiles are packed against the same end of the segment, in the same order, and the rest of the segment is empty. A tile created by a merge is never merged again in the same move. The score gains the value of every tile created by a merge.

Example on a line of 4 cells: `2 2 2 2` moved left becomes `4 4 . .` (score +8); moved right it becomes `. . 4 4` (score +8).

### Spawning

The generator is MINSTD: `state = state * 48271 mod 2147483647`, and `next()` returns the new state. `NewGame(seed)` starts with `state = seed mod 2147483647`, or `1` if that is 0.

A spawn first lists the candidate cells in row-major order (row 0 first, left to right): the cells that are empty and not walls. Then `i = (next() >> 8) mod (number of candidates)` picks the i-th candidate (0-based), and a second call decides the value: `1` normally, `2` when `(next() >> 8) mod 8 == 0`. The position is drawn before the value; nothing else ever calls `next()`. A new game spawns twice (two tiles) before the first move; every legal move spawns once, after the slide.

Check: with seed 1 the first four values of `next()` are 48271, 182605794, 1291394886, 1914720637.

## Rules of the game

The game is *over* when no move is legal. The first line of the board text carries ` WIN` when the largest tile is at least 64 and ` OVER` when the game is over (play simply continues after a win).

## API (package `triptych`)

```go
g := triptych.NewGame(seed uint32)
g.LegalMoves() []string          // the legal moves, in any order; empty when the game is over
g.Apply(move string) (string, error) // plays a legal move and returns the event; an error, and no change, otherwise
g.Render() string                // the board text (below)
g.Score() int
g.Over() bool
```

### Event returned by `Apply`

`+<points> spawn <row>,<col>=<value>`: the score gained by the move and the tile that spawned, for example `+9 spawn 2,0=1` (rows and columns from 0).

### `Render()`

The first line is `score <score> moves <moves>` followed by ` WIN` and/or ` OVER` when they apply (in that order). Then one line per row, no trailing newline at the end of the text. Every cell is written as its value (`.` for an empty cell, `#` for a wall), right-aligned to the width `w` = the number of digits of the largest tile on the board (at least 1), and the cells of a row are joined by a single space. Example (a board whose largest tile is 16):

```
score 90 moves 21
 .  2  .  1
16  .  4  .
 .  .  1  .
 2  .  .  .
```

## Tests

`go test ./...` replays the scenario files in `testdata/` (`adapter_test.go` shows how the API is called; the format is described at the top of `scenarios_test.go`).

start.README.md:
# Triptych

A sliding-tile merge game on a 5x5 board in the 2048 family, except that tiles merge in triples of 3. The engine is headless: a `Game`, its legal moves and exact text for every reply.

## The board

The board has 5 rows and 5 columns, numbered from 0, row 0 at the top. Walls (never entered by tiles, drawn `#`) stand at (row, column): (2,2). Every other cell is empty or holds a tile with a positive value; tile values are powers of 3 (1, 3, 9, ...).

## Moves

A move is one of the strings `L`, `R`, `U`, `D` (slide left, right, up, down; upper case only). A move is *legal* exactly when it changes the board; a move that would change nothing is illegal (and so is every other string). A legal move does, in this order: slide and merge (below), add the merge points to the score, count the move, spawn one tile.

### Sliding and merging

Lines move independently: every row for `L`/`R` and every column for `U`/`D` is a *line*, and the walls cut each line into *segments* (maximal runs of cells without a wall); segments are processed independently, tiles never cross a wall. Take a segment and read its tiles (skipping the empty cells) starting from the end nearest to the side the tiles move towards (the left end for `L`, the right end for `R`, the top for `U`, the bottom for `D`). Walk through that list from its start: if the next 3 tiles are all equal to some value `v`, they merge into one tile of value `3*v` and the walk continues after them; otherwise the tile stays as it is and the walk continues with the next one. The resulting tiles are packed against the same end of the segment, in the same order, and the rest of the segment is empty. A tile created by a merge is never merged again in the same move. The score gains the value of every tile created by a merge.

Example on a line of 5 cells: `1 1 1 1 3` moved left becomes `3 1 3 . .` (score +3); moved right it becomes `. . 1 3 3` (score +3).

### Spawning

The generator is MINSTD: `state = state * 48271 mod 2147483647`, and `next()` returns the new state. `NewGame(seed)` starts with `state = seed mod 2147483647`, or `1` if that is 0.

A spawn first lists the candidate cells in row-major order (row 0 first, left to right): the cells that are empty and not walls. Then `i = (next() >> 8) mod (number of candidates)` picks the i-th candidate (0-based), and a second call decides the value: `1` normally, `3` when `(next() >> 8) mod 8 == 0`. The position is drawn before the value; nothing else ever calls `next()`. A new game spawns twice (two tiles) before the first move; every legal move spawns once, after the slide.

Check: with seed 1 the first four values of `next()` are 48271, 182605794, 1291394886, 1914720637.

## Rules of the game

The game is *over* when no move is legal. The first line of the board text carries ` WIN` when the largest tile is at least 81 and ` OVER` when the game is over (play simply continues after a win).

## API (package `triptych`)

```go
g := triptych.NewGame(seed uint32)
g.LegalMoves() []string          // the legal moves, in any order; empty when the game is over
g.Apply(move string) (string, error) // plays a legal move and returns the event; an error, and no change, otherwise
g.Render() string                // the board text (below)
g.Score() int
g.Over() bool
```

### Event returned by `Apply`

`+<points> spawn <row>,<col>=<value>`: the score gained by the move and the tile that spawned, for example `+9 spawn 2,0=1` (rows and columns from 0).

### `Render()`

The first line is `score <score> moves <moves>` followed by ` WIN` and/or ` OVER` when they apply (in that order). Then one line per row, no trailing newline at the end of the text. Every cell is written as its value (`.` for an empty cell, `#` for a wall), right-aligned to the width `w` = the number of digits of the largest tile on the board (at least 1), and the cells of a row are joined by a single space. Example (a board whose largest tile is 81):

```
score 90 moves 21
 .  3  .  1  .
81  .  9  .  .
 .  .  #  .  .
 3  .  .  .  .
 .  .  .  .  .
```

## Tests

`go test ./...` replays the scenario files in `testdata/` (`adapter_test.go` shows how the API is called; the format is described at the top of `scenarios_test.go`).

start.README.md:
# Triptych

A sliding-tile merge game on a 4x4 board in the 2048 family, except that tiles merge in pairs of 2. The engine is headless: a `Game`, its legal moves and exact text for every reply.

## The board

The board has 4 rows and 4 columns, numbered from 0, row 0 at the top. Every other cell is empty or holds a tile with a positive value; tile values are powers of 2 (1, 2, 4, ...).

## Moves

A move is one of the strings `L`, `R`, `U`, `D` (slide left, right, up, down; upper case only). A move is *legal* exactly when it changes the board; a move that would change nothing is illegal (and so is every other string). A legal move does, in this order: slide and merge (below), add the merge points to the score, count the move, spawn one tile.

### Sliding and merging

Lines move independently: every row for `L`/`R` and every column for `U`/`D` is a *line*. Take a segment and read its tiles (skipping the empty cells) starting from the end nearest to the side the tiles move towards (the left end for `L`, the right end for `R`, the top for `U`, the bottom for `D`). Walk through that list from its start: if the next 2 tiles are all equal to some value `v`, they merge into one tile of value `2*v` and the walk continues after them; otherwise the tile stays as it is and the walk continues with the next one. The resulting tiles are packed against the same end of the segment, in the same order, and the rest of the segment is empty. A tile created by a merge is never merged again in the same move. The score gains the value of every tile created by a merge.

Example on a line of 4 cells: `2 2 2 2` moved left becomes `4 4 . .` (score +8); moved right it becomes `. . 4 4` (score +8).

### Spawning

The generator is MINSTD: `state = state * 48271 mod 2147483647`, and `next()` returns the new state. `NewGame(seed)` starts with `state = seed mod 2147483647`, or `1` if that is 0.

A spawn first lists the candidate cells in row-major order (row 0 first, left to right): the cells that are empty and not walls — but if at least one of them lies on the border of the board (row 0, row 3, column 0 or column 3), only the candidates on the border are kept. Then `i = (next() >> 8) mod (number of candidates)` picks the i-th candidate (0-based), and a second call decides the value: `1` normally, `2` when `(next() >> 8) mod 8 == 0`. The position is drawn before the value; nothing else ever calls `next()`. A new game spawns twice (two tiles) before the first move; every legal move spawns once, after the slide.

Check: with seed 1 the first four values of `next()` are 48271, 182605794, 1291394886, 1914720637.

## Rules of the game

The game is *over* when no move is legal. The first line of the board text carries ` WIN` when the largest tile is at least 32 and ` OVER` when the game is over (play simply continues after a win).

## API (package `triptych`)

```go
g := triptych.NewGame(seed uint32)
g.LegalMoves() []string          // the legal moves, in any order; empty when the game is over
g.Apply(move string) (string, error) // plays a legal move and returns the event; an error, and no change, otherwise
g.Render() string                // the board text (below)
g.Score() int
g.Over() bool
```

### Event returned by `Apply`

`+<points> spawn <row>,<col>=<value>`: the score gained by the move and the tile that spawned, for example `+9 spawn 2,0=1` (rows and columns from 0).

### `Render()`

The first line is `score <score> moves <moves>` followed by ` WIN` and/or ` OVER` when they apply (in that order). Then one line per row, no trailing newline at the end of the text. Every cell is written as its value (`.` for an empty cell, `#` for a wall), right-aligned to the width `w` = the number of digits of the largest tile on the board (at least 1), and the cells of a row are joined by a single space. Example (a board whose largest tile is 16):

```
score 90 moves 21
 .  2  .  1
16  .  4  .
 .  .  1  .
 2  .  .  .
```

## Tests

`go test ./...` replays the scenario files in `testdata/` (`adapter_test.go` shows how the API is called; the format is described at the top of `scenarios_test.go`).

start.README.md:
# Triptych

A sliding-tile merge game on a 5x5 board in the 2048 family, except that tiles merge in pairs of 2. The engine is headless: a `Game`, its legal moves and exact text for every reply.

## The board

The board has 5 rows and 5 columns, numbered from 0, row 0 at the top. Walls (never entered by tiles, drawn `#`) stand at (row, column): (1,3), (3,1). Every other cell is empty or holds a tile with a positive value; tile values are powers of 2 (1, 2, 4, ...).

## Moves

A move is one of the strings `L`, `R`, `U`, `D` (slide left, right, up, down; upper case only). A move is *legal* exactly when it changes the board; a move that would change nothing is illegal (and so is every other string). A legal move does, in this order: slide and merge (below), add the merge points to the score, count the move, spawn one tile.

### Sliding and merging

Lines move independently: every row for `L`/`R` and every column for `U`/`D` is a *line*, and the walls cut each line into *segments* (maximal runs of cells without a wall); segments are processed independently, tiles never cross a wall. Take a segment and read its tiles (skipping the empty cells) starting from the end nearest to the side the tiles move towards (the left end for `L`, the right end for `R`, the top for `U`, the bottom for `D`). Walk through that list from its start: if the next 2 tiles are all equal to some value `v`, they merge into one tile of value `2*v` and the walk continues after them; otherwise the tile stays as it is and the walk continues with the next one. The resulting tiles are packed against the same end of the segment, in the same order, and the rest of the segment is empty. A tile created by a merge is never merged again in the same move. The score gains the value of every tile created by a merge.

Example on a line of 5 cells: `2 2 2 2 4` moved left becomes `4 4 4 . .` (score +8); moved right it becomes `. . 4 4 4` (score +8).

### Spawning

The generator is MINSTD: `state = state * 48271 mod 2147483647`, and `next()` returns the new state. `NewGame(seed)` starts with `state = seed mod 2147483647`, or `1` if that is 0.

A spawn first lists the candidate cells in row-major order (row 0 first, left to right): the cells that are empty and not walls — but if at least one of them lies on the border of the board (row 0, row 4, column 0 or column 4), only the candidates on the border are kept. Then `i = (next() >> 8) mod (number of candidates)` picks the i-th candidate (0-based), and a second call decides the value: `1` normally, `2` when `(next() >> 8) mod 8 == 0`. The position is drawn before the value; nothing else ever calls `next()`. A new game spawns twice (two tiles) before the first move; every legal move spawns once, after the slide.

Check: with seed 1 the first four values of `next()` are 48271, 182605794, 1291394886, 1914720637.

## Rules of the game

The game is *over* when no move is legal. The first line of the board text carries ` WIN` when the largest tile is at least 64 and ` OVER` when the game is over (play simply continues after a win).

## API (package `triptych`)

```go
g := triptych.NewGame(seed uint32)
g.LegalMoves() []string          // the legal moves, in any order; empty when the game is over
g.Apply(move string) (string, error) // plays a legal move and returns the event; an error, and no change, otherwise
g.Render() string                // the board text (below)
g.Score() int
g.Over() bool
```

### Event returned by `Apply`

`+<points> spawn <row>,<col>=<value>`: the score gained by the move and the tile that spawned, for example `+9 spawn 2,0=1` (rows and columns from 0).

### `Render()`

The first line is `score <score> moves <moves>` followed by ` WIN` and/or ` OVER` when they apply (in that order). Then one line per row, no trailing newline at the end of the text. Every cell is written as its value (`.` for an empty cell, `#` for a wall), right-aligned to the width `w` = the number of digits of the largest tile on the board (at least 1), and the cells of a row are joined by a single space. Example (a board whose largest tile is 16):

```
score 90 moves 21
 .  2  .  1  .
16  .  4  #  .
 .  .  1  .  .
 2  #  .  .  .
 .  .  .  .  .
```

## Tests

`go test ./...` replays the scenario files in `testdata/` (`adapter_test.go` shows how the API is called; the format is described at the top of `scenarios_test.go`).

start.README.md:
# Triptych

A sliding-tile merge game on a 4x4 board in the 2048 family, except that tiles merge in triples of 3. The engine is headless: a `Game`, its legal moves and exact text for every reply.

## The board

The board has 4 rows and 4 columns, numbered from 0, row 0 at the top. Walls (never entered by tiles, drawn `#`) stand at (row, column): (0,2), (2,1). Every other cell is empty or holds a tile with a positive value; tile values are powers of 3 (1, 3, 9, ...).

## Moves

A move is one of the strings `L`, `R`, `U`, `D` (slide left, right, up, down; upper case only). A move is *legal* exactly when it changes the board; a move that would change nothing is illegal (and so is every other string). A legal move does, in this order: slide and merge (below), add the merge points to the score, count the move, spawn one tile.

### Sliding and merging

Lines move independently: every row for `L`/`R` and every column for `U`/`D` is a *line*, and the walls cut each line into *segments* (maximal runs of cells without a wall); segments are processed independently, tiles never cross a wall. Take a segment and read its tiles (skipping the empty cells) starting from the end nearest to the side the tiles move towards (the left end for `L`, the right end for `R`, the top for `U`, the bottom for `D`). Walk through that list from its start: if the next 3 tiles are all equal to some value `v`, they merge into one tile of value `3*v` and the walk continues after them; otherwise the tile stays as it is and the walk continues with the next one. The resulting tiles are packed against the same end of the segment, in the same order, and the rest of the segment is empty. A tile created by a merge is never merged again in the same move. The score gains the value of every tile created by a merge.

Example on a line of 4 cells: `1 1 1 1` moved left becomes `3 1 . .` (score +3); moved right it becomes `. . 1 3` (score +3).

### Spawning

The generator is MINSTD: `state = state * 48271 mod 2147483647`, and `next()` returns the new state. `NewGame(seed)` starts with `state = seed mod 2147483647`, or `1` if that is 0.

A spawn first lists the candidate cells in row-major order (row 0 first, left to right): the cells that are empty and not walls — but if at least one of them lies on the border of the board (row 0, row 3, column 0 or column 3), only the candidates on the border are kept. Then `i = (next() >> 8) mod (number of candidates)` picks the i-th candidate (0-based), and a second call decides the value: `1` normally, `3` when `(next() >> 8) mod 8 == 0`. The position is drawn before the value; nothing else ever calls `next()`. A new game spawns twice (two tiles) before the first move; every legal move spawns once, after the slide.

Check: with seed 1 the first four values of `next()` are 48271, 182605794, 1291394886, 1914720637.

## Rules of the game

The game is *over* when no move is legal. The first line of the board text carries ` WIN` when the largest tile is at least 27 and ` OVER` when the game is over (play simply continues after a win).

## API (package `triptych`)

```go
g := triptych.NewGame(seed uint32)
g.LegalMoves() []string          // the legal moves, in any order; empty when the game is over
g.Apply(move string) (string, error) // plays a legal move and returns the event; an error, and no change, otherwise
g.Render() string                // the board text (below)
g.Score() int
g.Over() bool
```

### Event returned by `Apply`

`+<points> spawn <row>,<col>=<value>`: the score gained by the move and the tile that spawned, for example `+9 spawn 2,0=1` (rows and columns from 0).

### `Render()`

The first line is `score <score> moves <moves>` followed by ` WIN` and/or ` OVER` when they apply (in that order). Then one line per row, no trailing newline at the end of the text. Every cell is written as its value (`.` for an empty cell, `#` for a wall), right-aligned to the width `w` = the number of digits of the largest tile on the board (at least 1), and the cells of a row are joined by a single space. Example (a board whose largest tile is 81):

```
score 90 moves 21
 .  3  #  1
81  .  9  .
 .  #  1  .
 3  .  .  .
```

## Tests

`go test ./...` replays the scenario files in `testdata/` (`adapter_test.go` shows how the API is called; the format is described at the top of `scenarios_test.go`).

start.README.md:
# Triptych

A sliding-tile merge game on a 5x5 board in the 2048 family, except that tiles merge in triples of 3. The engine is headless: a `Game`, its legal moves and exact text for every reply.

## The board

The board has 5 rows and 5 columns, numbered from 0, row 0 at the top. Walls (never entered by tiles, drawn `#`) stand at (row, column): (0,0), (2,2), (4,4). Every other cell is empty or holds a tile with a positive value; tile values are powers of 3 (1, 3, 9, ...).

## Moves

A move is one of the strings `L`, `R`, `U`, `D` (slide left, right, up, down; upper case only). A move is *legal* exactly when it changes the board; a move that would change nothing is illegal (and so is every other string). A legal move does, in this order: slide and merge (below), add the merge points to the score, count the move, spawn one tile.

### Sliding and merging

Lines move independently: every row for `L`/`R` and every column for `U`/`D` is a *line*, and the walls cut each line into *segments* (maximal runs of cells without a wall); segments are processed independently, tiles never cross a wall. Take a segment and read its tiles (skipping the empty cells) starting from the end nearest to the side the tiles move towards (the left end for `L`, the right end for `R`, the top for `U`, the bottom for `D`). Walk through that list from its start: if the next 3 tiles are all equal to some value `v`, they merge into one tile of value `3*v` and the walk continues after them; otherwise the tile stays as it is and the walk continues with the next one. The resulting tiles are packed against the same end of the segment, in the same order, and the rest of the segment is empty. A tile created by a merge is never merged again in the same move. The score gains the value of every tile created by a merge.

Example on a line of 5 cells: `1 1 1 1 3` moved left becomes `3 1 3 . .` (score +3); moved right it becomes `. . 1 3 3` (score +3).

### Spawning

The generator is MINSTD: `state = state * 48271 mod 2147483647`, and `next()` returns the new state. `NewGame(seed)` starts with `state = seed mod 2147483647`, or `1` if that is 0.

A spawn first lists the candidate cells in row-major order (row 0 first, left to right): the cells that are empty and not walls. Then `i = (next() >> 8) mod (number of candidates)` picks the i-th candidate (0-based), and a second call decides the value: `1` normally, `3` when `(next() >> 8) mod 8 == 0`. The position is drawn before the value; nothing else ever calls `next()`. A new game spawns twice (two tiles) before the first move; every legal move spawns once, after the slide.

Check: with seed 1 the first four values of `next()` are 48271, 182605794, 1291394886, 1914720637.

## Rules of the game

The game is *over* when no move is legal. The first line of the board text carries ` WIN` when the largest tile is at least 81 and ` OVER` when the game is over (play simply continues after a win).

## API (package `triptych`)

```go
g := triptych.NewGame(seed uint32)
g.LegalMoves() []string          // the legal moves, in any order; empty when the game is over
g.Apply(move string) (string, error) // plays a legal move and returns the event; an error, and no change, otherwise
g.Render() string                // the board text (below)
g.Score() int
g.Over() bool
```

### Event returned by `Apply`

`+<points> spawn <row>,<col>=<value>`: the score gained by the move and the tile that spawned, for example `+9 spawn 2,0=1` (rows and columns from 0).

### `Render()`

The first line is `score <score> moves <moves>` followed by ` WIN` and/or ` OVER` when they apply (in that order). Then one line per row, no trailing newline at the end of the text. Every cell is written as its value (`.` for an empty cell, `#` for a wall), right-aligned to the width `w` = the number of digits of the largest tile on the board (at least 1), and the cells of a row are joined by a single space. Example (a board whose largest tile is 81):

```
score 90 moves 21
 #  3  .  1  .
81  .  9  .  .
 .  .  #  .  .
 3  .  .  .  .
 .  .  .  .  #
```

## Tests

`go test ./...` replays the scenario files in `testdata/` (`adapter_test.go` shows how the API is called; the format is described at the top of `scenarios_test.go`).
